summary: Surveyed the checkout (Paper-Proof__paperproof, at reservoir-sources/Paper-Proof__paperproof): confirmed all 6 review-list files exist across four directories (_examples/demos/, _examples/workshop-tbilisi-2024/, extension/parsers/, lean/Services/, lean/). Paperproof is a VSCode extension/Lean-server tool that visualizes Lean tactic proofs as trees; its checkout mixes (a) tutorial/demo Lean files containing real theorem statements meant to showcase the visualizer, and (b) the tool's own Lean-side RPC/parser implementation that inspects Lean's InfoTree to extract tactic steps and goal states for the extension's UI. This matches the prior review RRV-dc05d5ab710d-r1's summary and its already-forced exclusions of `lakefile.lean`, `lean/Paperproof.lean`, `lean/Services.lean`, `lean/lakefile.lean`, and `lean/terminal.lean` as 'RPC/import/terminal wrappers and Lake build configuration around the service layer', with 'theorem-bearing examples remain retained'. Read `_examples/demos/Tutorial.lean` and `_examples/workshop-tbilisi-2024/3-Tutorial.lean` in full (near-identical tutorial files, 2448/2452 bytes): each contains six real theorem/example declarations (`simple_ex`, an unnamed `calc` example, an unnamed rewrite example, `finFunctionFinEquiv_single11`, three `inductive`+`theorem` pairs demonstrating `rcases`, `combs`) plus a seventh `append_assoc` theorem after an 'OPTIONS' comment block, all genuine mathematical statements (naturals, integers, `Fin`, inductive types, propositional logic) with real tactic proofs, written to demonstrate the visualizer -- theorem-bearing examples, retained per the prior review's own stated boundary. A declaration-keyword grep over the other 4 files found 63-75 raw matches each in `extension/parsers/v4.25.0.lean`/`v4.27.0.lean` and 28 in `lean/Services/BetterParser.lean`, but a targeted grep restricted to `theorem|lemma|example|axiom` (excluding `def`/`structure`/`instance`/`class`) showed every one of those matches is a string literal (`"theorem"`, `"axiom"`), a string comparison, a docstring, or a comment describing how the code classifies *other* declarations by introspecting Lean's `ConstantInfo`/`InfoTree` -- zero of the three files contains an actual `theorem`, `lemma`, `example`, or `axiom` command. Read all three files in full: `extension/parsers/v4.25.0.lean` and `extension/parsers/v4.27.0.lean` are near-duplicate, hand-maintained, Lean-version-pinned copies (per their own header comments, 'hand-maintained for Lean 4.25'/'4.27') of Paperproof's `GetTacticSubstring`/`GetTheorems`/`BetterParser`/`ppMcpGetProof` RPC service, namespaced `PaperproofMcp.Services` specifically so it does not clash with a real `import Paperproof`; `lean/Services/BetterParser.lean` is the corresponding non-version-pinned original under `Paperproof.Services`, importing `Services.GetTheorems`/`Services.GetTacticSubstring` and defining `BetterParser_Tree`/`BetterParser_SingleTactic`. All three hold only structures (`Hypothesis`, `GoalInfo`, `ProofStepPosition`, `ArgumentInfo`, `DeclarationInfo`, `PPInput`), `BEq`/`Hashable`/`FromJson`/`ToJson` instances, and `def`s that walk an `InfoTree`, format tactic substrings, and serve an `@[server_rpc_method]` RPC endpoint -- tooling/metaprogramming code with no formal mathematical declaration or proof of its own, the same 'service layer' class the prior review already excluded for `lean/Services.lean`, `lean/terminal.lean`, and `lean/Paperproof.lean`; extending that established, content-verified class to these 3 newly-added/changed files under FILTER-004(1). By contrast, read `lean/Tests.lean` in full (9649 bytes): it imports `Services.BetterParser` and Mathlib, defines a custom `#assert_parser in <command>` elaborator and `#guard_msgs`-checked format helpers to regression-test the parser, but the body of the file also contains 8 real `theorem`/`example` declarations with complete, non-`sorry` proofs over natural numbers, sets, and propositional logic (`simple`, `commutativityOfIntersections`, `spawned`, `test_intro_multi`, `test_intros_multi`, `test_simp_rw`, `test_foo`, an unnamed `example`, `test_simpa`, `test_simpa_nested_by`) -- read several of these (lines 58-80, 240-260, 425-470) and confirmed each is a genuine, complete theorem statement and proof, not a stub; since this file holds real formal-mathematics content alongside its test-harness code, it does not meet FILTER-004(1)'s content-invariant and is retained under the default.
